questions.question: What does abstraction hide from the caller?
options: How a task is carried out
questions.explanation: Abstraction shows what an object can do and hides how it does it inside concrete classes.

questions.question: Which two Java features are used to achieve abstraction?
questions.explanation: Abstract classes and interfaces declare methods that concrete classes must implement.

questions.question: abstract class Sensor { abstract int read(); } ... Sensor s = new Sensor(); Why does this fail to compile?
options: An abstract class cannot be instantiated with new
questions.explanation: You create objects of concrete subclasses and store them in a Sensor variable instead.

questions.question: abstract class Heater { abstract void warm(); } class RoomHeater extends Heater { void cool() { } } Why does RoomHeater fail to compile?
options: cool() is not allowed in a subclass
It does not implement warm() and is not marked abstract
questions.explanation: A concrete subclass must implement every inherited abstract method, or be declared abstract itself.

questions.question: What does this print? abstract class Fan { abstract String spin(); void run() { System.out.print("[" + spin() + "]"); } } class CeilingFan extends Fan { String spin() { return "slow"; } } ... new CeilingFan().run();
questions.explanation: run() is written in the abstract class but calls spin() on the real object, which is a CeilingFan.

questions.question: Which statement about abstract classes is true?
options: They can have constructors and normal methods
Every method in them must be abstract
questions.explanation: An abstract class can mix fields, constructors, finished methods and abstract methods.

questions.question: How does abstraction differ from encapsulation?
options: They are two names for the same idea
Abstraction needs private fields; encapsulation needs interfaces
Abstraction hides implementation; encapsulation hides and protects data
Encapsulation only works with abstract classes
questions.explanation: Abstraction simplifies use through a contract, while encapsulation controls access to an object's state.

questions.question: abstract class Plug { abstract void connect() { } } Why does this fail to compile?
options: Abstract classes need a main method
An abstract method cannot have a body
questions.explanation: An abstract method ends with a semicolon. Remove abstract to give it a body instead.

questions.question: What does this print? interface Dimmer { int level(); } class Lamp implements Dimmer { public int level() { return 40; } } ... Dimmer d = new Lamp(); System.out.println(d.level() + 10);
questions.explanation: The call through the interface runs Lamp's level(), which returns 40, and 40 + 10 is 50.

questions.question: Can a class be declared abstract even if it has no abstract methods?
options: No, it must have at least one abstract method
Only if it also implements an interface
Only if all its fields are final
Yes, it simply cannot be instantiated
questions.explanation: The abstract keyword alone blocks direct instances, which is useful for base classes meant only to be extended.
